Inherited a Home With a Reverse Mortgage? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is and work with the lender and title company on the payoff. Tell us about the house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Texas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

When the last borrower on a Texas reverse mortgage dies, the loan becomes due, and HUD says an FHA-insured HECM must be satisfied within 30 days of the borrower's death, with possible 90-day extensions if heirs are actively trying to sell or repay. This guide summarizes the Texas Constitution's reverse mortgage rules and HUD's heirs flyer. The HUD document is from 2019, so confirm current deadlines with the lender.

When a Texas reverse mortgage comes due

Under Texas Constitution Article XVI, Sec. 50(k)(6), no payment of principal or interest is required until one of these happens:

  • all borrowers have died;
  • the homestead is sold or otherwise transferred;
  • all borrowers stop living there for more than 12 consecutive months without prior written lender approval;
  • the borrower defaults on repairs and maintenance, taxes or assessments, or insurance, commits actual fraud, or fails to maintain lien priority.

A Texas reverse mortgage must go to a borrower who, or whose spouse, is 62 or older, and it carries no recourse for personal liability against each owner and each owner's spouse (Sec. 50(k)(2) and (3)). Interest can accrue and compound during the loan term as the agreement provides (Sec. 50(m)).

What heirs can do

HUD's flyer for heirs of an FHA-insured HECM says:

  • The loan must be satisfied within 30 days of the borrower's death. The lender may approve 90-day extensions with documentation that the estate or heirs are actively trying to sell or repay.
  • If the balance is more than the home is worth, the estate or heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value, and the lender accepts the net proceeds as satisfaction of the loan.
  • Heirs who want to keep the home must pay the balance in full. Property taxes and insurance stay the estate's responsibility until title transfers.
  • A non-borrowing spouse may qualify for special provisions that postpone repayment, but must give the lender a Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification within 30 days of the last borrower's death, among other requirements.

Contact the lender right away. The HUD FHA Resource Center number on the flyer is (800) 225-5342. Heirs also need to settle who has authority to sell, which depends on whether there is a will. See the Texas probate process and affidavit of heirship.

Inherited a home with a HECM?
We buy as-is and can close quickly, with no commission. The title company pays off the lender from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

If the lender wants to foreclose

The lender cannot begin foreclosure until it gives notice that a ground exists and gives the borrower at least 30 days (20 days for a lien-priority default) to fix the problem, pay the debt from a sale or other sources, or give a deed in lieu of foreclosure (Sec. 50(k)(10)). Foreclosure needs a court order, except where the ground is that all borrowers have died or the home was sold or transferred (Sec. 50(k)(11)). See the Texas foreclosure process.

What we could not confirm

  • Any Texas Finance Code provision on reverse mortgages.
  • Whether HUD's later guidance changed the 2019 flyer's deadlines or extension rules, and how many extensions a lender can grant.
  • How the Texas 30-day and 20-day foreclosure notice interacts with HUD's 30-day payoff timeline.

How to sell a house in Texas when there is a reverse mortgage

  1. Call the HECM lender, ask for a payoff statement and confirm the deadline in writing.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Texas house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Texas.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Texas

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Texas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Texas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Texas

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Texas reverse mortgage FAQ

How long do heirs have to deal with a HECM?

HUD says the loan must be satisfied within 30 days of the borrower's death, and the lender may approve 90-day extensions with documentation that the estate or heirs are actively trying to sell or repay.

Can heirs sell for less than the loan balance?

HUD says that if the balance exceeds the home's value, heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value, and the lender accepts the net proceeds as satisfaction of the loan.

What makes a Texas reverse mortgage due?

The death of all borrowers, a sale or transfer, absence for more than 12 consecutive months without lender approval, or a default on taxes, insurance, maintenance or lien priority, or fraud (Const. art. XVI, Sec. 50(k)(6)).

Can a surviving spouse who is not on the loan stay?

HUD says special provisions may postpone repayment, but the spouse must give the lender a certification within 30 days of the last borrower's death, among other requirements.

Who gets a lien and when

A person has a lien if, under a contract with the owner or the owner's agent, trustee, contractor or subcontractor, the person furnishes labor or materials to build or repair an improvement (Sec. 53.021). Property Code Sec. 41.001(b)(3) says work and material encumbrances can be properly fixed on homestead property only if contracted in writing as Sec. 53.254(a), (b) and (c) provide.

For a homestead, a lien affidavit must carry the notice "THIS IS NOT A LIEN. THIS IS ONLY AN AFFIDAVIT CLAIMING A LIEN" in at least 10-point boldface at the top of the page, and the owner notice must include the statutory statement about reserving 10 percent (Sec. 53.254(f) and (g)).

Filing and suit deadlines

  • Original contractor, residential project: file the lien affidavit with the county clerk by the 15th day of the third month after the month the work was completed, terminated or abandoned (Sec. 53.052(a)).
  • Other claimants, residential project: the 15th day of the third month after the later of the month they last provided labor or materials (Sec. 53.052(c)).
  • Where: the county where the improvements are located (Sec. 53.052(e)).
  • Suit to foreclose: not later than the first anniversary of the last day the claimant could file the affidavit, extendable to the second anniversary of filing by a recorded written agreement made before the period expires (Sec. 53.158).
  • Owner retainage: the owner must reserve 10 percent of the contract price or work value during the work and for 30 days after completion (Sec. 53.101(a)).

Getting a lien released

Within 10 days after a written request, a claimant paid with collected funds must furnish a recordable release (Sec. 53.152). A filed lien can also end by a recorded release, by the claimant failing to sue within the Sec. 53.158 period, by a recorded final judgment, by a bond, or by a recorded order removing the lien if no bond or deposit is filed within 30 days (Sec. 53.157). In a suit, a party can file a verified summary motion to remove a lien, and for a homestead the grounds include no contract executed or filed as Sec. 53.254 requires (Sec. 53.160).

What we could not confirm

  • How an unreleased lien affects a closing and how title companies handle it. No statute text we opened says so.
  • The notice-of-claim deadlines in Secs. 53.056 and 53.057, and whether the 2025 legislature changed Chapter 53.

A Texas landlord cannot lock a tenant out to show or sell a house, and a violation carries a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000. That rule is in Property Code Sec. 92.0081. This guide summarizes the sections of Chapters 91 and 92 we opened that matter when you sell a rented home. We did not find statute text that says a lease survives a sale, so we do not state it.

Ending a month-to-month tenancy

Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy by notice. For a rent period of at least one month, it ends on the later of the day stated in the notice or one month after notice is given (Property Code Sec. 91.001(a) and (b)). A signed agreement can set a different notice period (Sec. 91.001(e)). If a tenancy ends mid-period, the tenant owes rent only to the termination date (Sec. 91.001(d)). Eviction follows its own rules. See the Texas eviction process.

Lockouts and entry

A landlord may not intentionally keep a tenant out of the premises except by judicial process, unless the cause is bona fide repairs, construction or an emergency, removing the contents of abandoned premises, or a lawful lock change for delinquent rent (Sec. 92.0081(b)). A lock-change notice must be mailed locally by the fifth calendar day, or hand-delivered or posted by the third calendar day, before the change (Sec. 92.0081(d)(3)). A violating landlord owes a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000, actual damages, court costs and attorney's fees (Sec. 92.0081(h)).

We did not find a Chapter 92 provision that sets an entry notice period for showings. Entry rules depend on the lease.

Own a rental you want to sell?
We buy tenant-occupied and vacant houses as-is, with no commission.
Get My Cash Offer →

Repairs continue during a sale

A landlord must make a diligent effort to repair a condition that materially affects health or safety once the tenant gives notice and is current on rent (Sec. 92.052(a)), and seven days is presumed a reasonable time (Sec. 92.056(d)). If a new landlord acquires title in good faith by foreclosure, deed in lieu or a bona fide purchase by general warranty deed without knowledge of a tenant's repair notice, the tenant's right to terminate stays in place. For other conditions the tenant must give the new landlord written notice once told the new landlord's name and address (Sec. 92.0562(g)). A new landlord who violates that subsection owes a civil penalty of one month's rent plus $2,000, actual damages and attorney's fees.

Security deposits when you sell

The buyer becomes liable for security deposits from the date title is acquired and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact dollar amount (Sec. 92.105). See Texas security deposit rules.

title: Texas Security Deposit Rules: Refunds, Penalties and What Happens When You Sell
content:
Texas Security Deposit Rules: Refunds, Penalties and What Happens When You Sell

Cash Home Buyers in Texas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling a Rental? Get a Cash Offer

We buy rentals as-is. Tell us about the property and the tenants.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Texas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

A Texas landlord must refund a security deposit on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises, and a landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith owes $100, three times the amount wrongfully withheld, and the tenant's attorney's fees. Those rules are in Property Code Secs. 92.103 and 92.109. This guide also covers what changes when the owner sells.

Refund and deduction rules

  • A security deposit is an advance of money, other than a rental application deposit or advance rent, meant mainly to secure performance under a dwelling lease (Sec. 92.102).
  • Refund the deposit on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises (Sec. 92.103(a)).
  • A landlord may deduct damages and charges the tenant is legally liable for, but may not keep any part for normal wear and tear (Sec. 92.104(a) and (b)).
  • If any deposit is kept, the landlord must give the balance with a written description and itemized list of deductions, unless the tenant owes rent at surrender and there is no controversy about the rent (Sec. 92.104(c)).
  • A refund or accounting counts as made if it is mailed and postmarked on or before the due date (Sec. 92.1041).
  • The landlord does not have to return the deposit or send the itemization until the tenant gives a written forwarding address, but the tenant does not lose the refund just for failing to give one (Sec. 92.107).

Penalties

A landlord who keeps a deposit in bad faith is liable for $100, three times the portion wrongfully withheld and the tenant's reasonable attorney's fees. A landlord who in bad faith fails to give the itemized list gives up the right to withhold any deposit or to sue the tenant for damage, and owes attorney's fees (Sec. 92.109). The landlord has the burden to prove the retention was reasonable, and failing to refund or itemize by the 30th day is presumed bad faith. A tenant may not withhold the last month's rent on the ground that the deposit covers it, and a bad-faith violation makes the tenant liable for three times the rent withheld plus attorney's fees (Sec. 92.108).

When the owner sells

If the owner's interest ends by sale, assignment, death, receivership, bankruptcy or otherwise, the new owner is liable for deposits from the date title is acquired and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact dollar amount (Sec. 92.105(a) and (b)). The former owner stays liable for a deposit received while owner until the new owner has received it or assumed liability, unless a written contract says otherwise. A mortgage lienholder who takes title by foreclosure is excepted (Sec. 92.105(b-1) and (c)). Landlords must keep accurate deposit records (Sec. 92.106). See selling a rented house in Texas.

How to sell a house in Texas when there is a deposit to transfer

  1. Add up every tenant's deposit and put the amounts in the closing paperwork so they transfer correctly.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Texas house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Texas.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Texas

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Texas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Texas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Texas

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Texas security deposit FAQ

How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit?

On or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the premises (Property Code Sec. 92.103(a)).

Can a landlord keep a deposit for normal wear and tear?

No. A landlord may not retain any portion for normal wear and tear (Sec. 92.104(b)).

What is the penalty for keeping a deposit in bad faith?

$100, three times the portion wrongfully withheld and the tenant's reasonable attorney's fees (Sec. 92.109(a)).

Who owes the deposit after a sale?

The new owner is liable from the date title is acquired and must give the tenant a signed statement with the exact amount (Sec. 92.105).
